newsitem.title: FRANCE: France Telecom worth 150-180 bln ffr-AMRO.
newsitem.headline: France Telecom worth 150-180 bln ffr-AMRO.

text.p: ABN Amro Hoare Govett analyst James Downie put a value of 150 billion to 180 billion francs on France Telecom SA, due to be partially privatised next month.

According to a document obtained by Reuters, Downie said that at the top end of the range France Telecom "will still be inexpensively priced valued in Price/Earnings terms (at 12.8 times 1997 earnings), and on the basis of EV/EBITDA multiples (at 4.4 times 1997 EBITDATA)."

Downie used a discounted cash flow methodology taking a discount rate of 11.5 percent and an exit multiple of three. He also used a dividend discount model with a discount rate of 10 percent and assumed dividend growth rate after 2006 of four percent per year.

"We expect France Telecom's normalised net earnings to grow at around 11 percent per year over the next five years. This figure has been adjusted to strip out one-off accounting changes in 1996," the document said.

"The company is strongly cash generative, and should be able to pay down debt from 107 billion francs in 1996 to 50 billion francs in 2001, reducing gearing from 136 percent to 41 percent in the process," he added.
ABN Amro is not a lead-bank in the placement syndicate, which is being coordinated by BNP BNPP PA and Paribas PARI.PA, but the syndicate has not yet been completed.
A value of 150 billion to 180 billion francs would mean a share price of between 150 and 170 francs.
Fund managers reported that a number of banks were contacting them with analysts' estimates, but many banks and brokers declined to comment to journalists.
Under the placement rules, analysts are free to publish their value estimates this week following a March 20 briefing by the company.

BZW in June 1996 published a document which roughly valued France Telecom at between 150 billion and 200 billion francs. Fund managers said BZW was now "more towards 150 billion than 200 billion". BZW declined to comment.

The Finance Ministry will on May 5 announce a price range for France Telecom after which there will be a three week reservation period for private investors. On May 26 the final price will be set and the Initial Public Offering will take place between May 27 and June 3.
